holisticNarrative.summary:
The evidence package for BESTCare is unusual because it combines two very different documentation postures. On one hand, the native b.10 artifact is extremely concise: it names CSV and Oracle DMP and asserts single/patient-population export capabilities, but it does not publish the table inventory, field dictionary, relationship map, or sample files needed for dependable migration engineering. On the other hand, the linked API portal is richly documented for US Core FHIR and bulk export operations, with concrete endpoint patterns, request parameters, and example payloads.

For EHI assessment under designated-record-set logic, this creates a practical asymmetry. The standards path is technically implementable and clinically meaningful, but likely not sufficient alone for full designated-record-set extraction in a large hospital system where billing and other patient-decision records matter. The native path may in fact cover these areas, but the current artifacts do not allow that claim to be validated. As a result, the right posture is neither "no export" nor "high fidelity"; it is usable but partially evidenced, with the largest uncertainty concentrated in native export semantics rather than endpoint availability.
standoutObservations: Native export claims are broad (including population-wide data) but structurally opaque.
FHIR documentation quality is materially better than native export documentation.
The b.10 PDF directly links to API portal docs, suggesting operational overlap between b.10 and g(10) paths.

notableFacts: The b.10 PDF explicitly states single-patient export can be run "without developer assistance."
The same PDF claims multi-patient export can export "all the data for a patient population."
Native file formats named in b.10 documentation are CSV and Oracle DMP.
The linked Multi Patient API guide documents `/Patient/$export`, `/Group/[id]/$export`, and `/$export` with `application/fhir+ndjson` output.
CapabilityStatement advertises 26 supported FHIR resource types on an R4 server named `ezfhirstation-us-core-usa-aurora`.
